question.text: Under the normal rolling settlement cycle prescribed by SEBI/NSE for equity trades in Indian stock exchanges, settlement is currently completed on:

answer.text: T+1 (trade date plus one business day)
T+2 (trade date plus two business days)
T+3 (trade date plus three business days)

explanation.text: The Logic: Under the normal rolling settlement cycle, Indian equity trades settle on T+1 — i.e., the next business day after the trade date. India moved from T+2 to T+1 in 2023, making it among the fastest equity settlement markets in the world. The Trap: NSE has also introduced an optional T+0 (same-day) settlement window for a limited list of eligible stocks alongside T+1. Because of this, the original unqualified "currently" wording made both T+0 and T+1 defensible. The revised stem restricts the question to the normal rolling settlement cycle, under which T+1 is uniquely correct. T+2 and T+3 are historical or non-Indian cycles. Note: Source: NISM-Series-X-A Investment Adviser (Level 1), June 2025, pp. 118-120, 194; cross-referenced with NSE equity-market settlement-cycle and NSE T+0 pages. The stem has been narrowed to the normal rolling cycle to remove ambiguity with the optional T+0 facility.
